$comment: Warden seat permission profile (ForgeOs-21f.1). Loaded by fort/scripts/warden.sh with --setting-sources '' so this file is the ONLY permission source. The launcher also restricts the tool set to Bash,Read,Grep,Glob (no Edit/Write/Task), sets cwd to a scratch copy, and adds the checkout(s) via --add-dir. The seat has ZERO write permissions: the launcher records the verdict (bd comment --file from the session log) and emits the review.verdict event. IMPORTANT, verified 2026-08-03: commands absent from the allow list are NOT reliably denied — Claude Code's built-in classifier auto-allows some read-only commands (sed ran; awk and python failed shut; mutating forms like sed -i and redirection were refused). Treat the allow list as convenience, the deny list as the boundary, and assume unknown read-only commands may run. Hence the broad Bash(*.env*) deny; obfuscated-path reads remain for 21f.4 to probe. Deny globs match the whole command line INCLUDING quoted arguments — prose containing a denied pattern trips the rule. ForgeOs-8yad (Regent edict, 2026-09-01): standing order 8 mandates absolute paths, and this list allowed ONLY the relative verify.sh spelling, so the profile actively refused the form the charter requires — Tova got there on her third attempt, and her point was that a Warden who did not would be tempted to substitute a hand-rolled build-and-test and report it as the verifier. The absolute forms added are the SCRATCH ones, /tmp/warden-<suffix>/ (respelled 2026-09-12 under ForgeOs-nv0j to /home/justin/.local/share/proofdelve/warden/<suffix>/, where warden.sh now puts the copy; the wildcard is one path segment, the bead suffix), and that is deliberate: warden.sh sets cwd to that rsync copy, and verify.sh scores the tree it lives in (ForgeOs-afdr), so allowing the /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs/ spelling would have invited a green measured against MAIN and reported as the candidate's gate — the same 'the gate said yes without running on the thing' family 8yad was filed under. ForgeOs-dijj.1 (same edict): Bash(find *) was REMOVED rather than narrowed. find reaches -delete and -exec straight past the Bash(rm *) deny because the command word is find, and these rules are prefix globs that cannot constrain a trailing argument, so no narrower allow entry expresses 'read-only find' — and a deny list enumerating dangerous spellings is exactly the pattern ForgeOs-21f.8 measured as defeatable 6/6. Removal is the only narrowing this mechanism actually supports; rg, grep, ls, stat and file cover the read need. Blast radius was bounded to the scratch cwd, not the repo, which is why it was P2 and not P1. CORRECTED 2026-09-18 (ForgeOs-25rz, Regent sitting B, Overseer present; the finding is Tova Marrowassay's number 4 on ForgeOs-v1x3, MEASURED from inside her live profile on 2026-09-02, not reasoned): the two sentences above overstate what the removal closed. With Bash(find *) already gone, plain find ... -name README.md still RAN (the classifier auto-allows it, exactly as the first paragraph of this comment warns), and find ... -delete and find ... -exec were both REFUSED by Claude Code's own classifier ('find with -delete executes commands or modifies files, cannot be auto-allowed by a Bash(find:*) prefix rule'). So on this build the mutating predicates were never reachable through the allow rule, and 'the only narrowing this mechanism actually supports' describes a narrowing that could not be measured because nothing was open to narrow. What the removal IS: defence in depth against that classifier behaviour changing between versions, which a permission profile must not rest on; she endorsed keeping it out and lost no tool. fort/advisories.md's ADV-0002 row carries the same re-measurement (85fb437b, the Mayor's half). ForgeOs-riev (Regent edict, 2026-09-04): the Write(**) deny was REMOVED because it is INERT and says so on every launch. Claude Code prints 'Permission deny rule ...: Write(X) is not matched by file permission checks -- only Edit(path) rules are' into $log.err, 672 bytes of it, on every Warden launch into a file nobody reads (fortkit-yowr, measured across all three forts). Nothing is newly exposed: Edit(**) above already binds the Write tool, the launcher does not grant Write at all (--tools Bash,Read,Grep,Glob), and the kernel mask is the real boundary. A rule that silently does nothing is worse than no rule, because a reader counts it as protection. NOT DONE HERE, and deliberately: the fourteen allow entries of the shape Bash(git -C * SUBCOMMAND*) and Bash(bd -C * SUBCOMMAND*) put a wildcard BEFORE the subcommand, so a -c core.pager=COMMAND option slipped into that gap still matches the rule and no deny matches git -c under any spelling. Whether a session REACHES execution through one of them was never measured, and an allow rule matching is necessary but not sufficient, so narrowing them on reasoning alone would be a guess about a boundary. warden.sh now carries WARDEN_SMOKE probe 12, which settles it by running the command; narrow these only on that measurement. NARROWED 2026-09-04, same edict, on a MEASUREMENT of the product's own rule checker rather than on reasoning: scratch settings files carrying one rule each were run through claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --setting-sources '' --settings <f>. Bash(git -C * worktree list*) IS flagged; git -C * with log, diff, show, status, blame, rev-parse, rev-list, ls-files and branch, and every bd -C * form, are NOT; Bash(git -C <absolute path> worktree list*) is NOT; and Bash(git -C <root>-worktrees/* worktree list*) still IS. So the discriminator is a MULTI-WORD subcommand after the wildcard, not the wildcard as such, and the docket's proposed broadening to all fourteen was wrong -- its own caveat said to check this before acting on it, and checking is what falsified it. Only line 15 is narrowed, to the explicit root spelling. That loses the Warden nothing: git worktree list reports the whole repository from any tree in it, so the -worktrees glob was never needed, and it is the one replacement the checker still rejects. Launch stderr drops from 672 bytes to 0. ForgeOs-4778 (Regent edict, 2026-09-11, the fortkit-y7no exposure): Bash(systemd-run*) and Bash(systemctl*) DENIED. /run/user/1000/bus is reachable inside every seat mask, so systemd-run --user from inside a mask starts an UNMASKED host process (measured from the Mayor mask on 2026-09-10 and again 2026-09-11: 30 mounts against 81, the inode-masked secret at its full byte count, fort/scripts writable). This deny is the INTERIM tool-layer control until the capital's lib fix lands; it binds the command word only, so an absolute-path spelling (/usr/bin/systemd-run) passes it, measured and recorded on the bead as the known residual rather than enumerated into the list (ForgeOs-21f.8). For this seat it is belt: the launcher runs -p under defaultMode default, so an unlisted command is already refused, and the deny makes the refusal durable rather than allow-list-shaped (FRAGILE in the probe suite's vocabulary). ForgeOs-riev (Regent edict, 2026-09-11, the narrowing): THE THIRTEEN WILDCARD-BEFORE-SUBCOMMAND ALLOW RULES ARE GONE. Tova Marrowassay established by execution (2026-09-04, from inside a real Warden mask) that `git -C <root> -c core.fsmonitor=id status` matched Bash(git -C * status*) and RAN id, so the allow rules of that shape granted arbitrary command execution as the seat, past a deny list that stops Bash(rm *) but not git -c core.fsmonitor='rm ...' status. The reason they were not narrowed on 2026-09-04 was that the Warden needs the candidate WORKTREE path too, and the only prefix-glob spelling covering /home/justin/dev/ForgeOs-worktrees/ is a wildcard. THE ANSWER IS THAT THIS FILE NO LONGER HAS TO SPELL IT: every git -C and bd -C rule here names the root checkout explicitly, and fort/scripts/warden.sh RENDERS this file per review -- for a candidate tree that is not the root it adds a twin of every `git -C <root> ...` rule with the candidate's exact path substituted, and passes the result to claude as an inline --settings JSON string rather than a file, so the seat cannot edit what it was launched under. The explicit spelling leaves no gap between -C and the subcommand for an option to sit in, so `git -C <root> -c KEY=CMD status` matches nothing and is refused under defaultMode default. bd -C is rendered for the root only: bd always targets the main repo's .beads and the Warden's own prompt says so. No deny rule for -c or --exec-path was added: with no gap to match, a deny would be the enumerate-the-dangerous-spelling shape ForgeOs-21f.8 measured as defeatable, and `-c` is a legitimate `git log`/`git show` option (combined diff) a deny would also refuse. MEASURED, not reasoned: WARDEN_SMOKE probe 12 runs exactly Tova's command and reports refused/executed; see the bead for the run. ForgeOs-51x1 (Overseer ruling 2026-09-16, option (a)): the Edit(**) deny is REMOVED so warden.sh can grant Edit(<scratch>/**) per review with the exact scratch path -- deny beats allow, so the two could not coexist. No static Edit allow is added: the grant exists only in the rendered per-review settings, and an Edit outside the scratch path is unlisted, which is a refusal under defaultMode default in a -p session; the kernel mask keeps the checkout read-only regardless. Measured by WARDEN_SMOKE probe 14 (scratch edit succeeds; root Edit and root sed -i both refused). The reason the seat needs this at all: every criterion of the form 'rewire X, run, paste the RED' was taken on faith because no tool on the seat could mutate its own scratch copy (measured 2026-09-15, three reviews in one afternoon). ForgeOs-bsw1 (Regent sitting B, 2026-09-18, Overseer present; Tova Marrowassay's finding 6 on ForgeOs-v1x3): THE SECRETS-SPELLING SYNC RULE, written here because this is one of the three lists it binds. A secrets spelling lives in THREE places and an edit to any one of them touches all three: (1) this file's deny list (Read and Bash rules; the only permission source of the Warden seat, since warden.sh passes --setting-sources ''), (2) .claude/settings.json (Edit, Read and Bash rules for the Mayor seat), (3) fort/scripts/forge.sh's deny_table (the Codex policy layer for the Forge). ForgeOs-szai added five spellings, the editor forms of .env.staging.local (..env*, .#*env*, #*env*#, .*env*.sw*, *env*~), to (2) and (3) on 2026-09-02 and this list never got them; Read(**/.env*) cannot match ..env.staging.local.kate-swp, and the broad Bash(*.env*) misses only env.staging.local~, the backup form with no leading dot, hence the one Bash(*env*~*) beside it. This is the CONVENIENCE layer and the P3 says so: the kernel masks all six spellings for every seat (SECRET_GLOBS, lib/seat-sandbox.sh), verified by her, and the tool-layer deny is the second line by the charter's own design (ADV-0004: ask which layer holds a control). ForgeOs-mskx + ForgeOs-rydv (Regent sitting B, 2026-09-18, Overseer present, gate 6): THE EXECUTION GRANTS. Over a week of reviews the seat measured, and the Mayor tabulated on ForgeOs-mskx, what it could not execute: node (mskx), npm --prefix tools/keep test (6vpe), python3 (b0vj.21), sed (52gy), bash <harness> (7dq7; ADV-0011). ForgeOs-8zb7 established that a control is shown to DISCRIMINATE by inversion, and a reviewer who can never execute an instrument can never invert it: every inversion on the board was the Forge's paste checked by her reading, with the faith boundary stated each time, which is why nothing false reached the record and also why the claims were weaker than they read. ADDED HERE: Bash(node *), Bash(python3 *), Bash(sed *), Bash(npm --prefix tools/keep test*). RENDERED PER REVIEW by warden.sh (ForgeOs-riev's mechanism): the tools/keep twin at the exact scratch path, and for every scripts/*-harness.sh present in the candidate tree two rules naming that ONE script by its exact absolute scratch path (bash <path>* and <path>*), enumerated from the tree at launch and counted fail-closed (exit 67 on a miscount), so this file never carries a harness list that goes stale and no rule is a glob over scripts/ (ADV-0002's reasoning, criterion 2 of rydv). Every rule scored 0 on the vendor checker; Bash(git -C * worktree list*) as the positive control scored 1; launch stderr stays 0 bytes. WHY THIS IS NOT THE WIDENING IT READS AS, measured 2026-09-18 in the real Warden mask built from warden.sh's own lines: since ForgeOs-51x1 the seat may Edit its scratch copy, <scratch>/fort/scripts is WRITABLE inside her mask, and <scratch>/fort/scripts/verify.sh has been on this allow list since ForgeOs-8yad -- so the seat could already run arbitrary shell as itself by rewriting that one file and running it. The policy layer withheld execution in convenience only. This comment's first paragraph has said since 2026-08-03 that the allow list is convenience, the deny list the accident belt, and the kernel mask the boundary; it still is. What the deny list still buys is threat 1, agent accident: the sed *e* command and python's os.system are arbitrary execution, and they are arbitrary execution INSIDE a mask in which the real checkout, every other tree, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and the secrets file are read-only or /dev/null (the session-bus residual, fortkit-y7no, is reachable through /usr/bin/systemd-run already and is not widened in kind). rydv criterion 1, answered before granting: the transitive route (verify.sh runs four harnesses) is NOT sufficient, because a harness cannot be run alone, against a variant, or inverted through it, and step 2 of ForgeOs-8zb7 is exactly that. The variant route needs no env-prefix rule: harnesses default to the launcher beside them and her scratch launcher is hers to edit. ForgeOs-6d8h (Regent sitting AD, 2026-09-18, Overseer present, gate 6; Tova Marrowassay finding 3 on ForgeOs-mskx, then two instances on the Mayor within the hour): THE Bash(*env*~*) DENY IS REMOVED from this list and from .claude/settings.json. A Bash deny is a substring match over the WHOLE command line, prose included, so that rule refused a grep for the word environment against a tilde-spelled home path, the Mayor's bd create filing the finding, and the Mayor's heredoc writing the next docket. MEASURED before removal with a one-rule scratch settings file under claude -p: `grep -c environment ~/dev/fortkit/README.md` REFUSED with the rule present, EXECUTED without it; positive control `cat /tmp/nowhere/.env.staging.local~` still REFUSED by Bash(*.env*) alone. What the removed rule was for -- the backup spelling with NO leading dot, env.staging.local~ -- is not one any editor produces from a dot-prefixed file; every backup and swap form keeps the basename, so Bash(*.env*) covers the dotted tilde form and the ten Read() forms (filename globs, precise, kept) cover the rest. The three-list sync rule above still binds: the Read forms and forge.sh's deny_table path globs are untouched; only the Bash substring rule leaves, from both Bash lists. The kernel masks *env*~ for every seat regardless (SECRET_GLOBS).
